blocks.text: The **National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)** is the **umbrella organisation for all retail payments** in India. It was set up with the guidance and support of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and the **Indian Banks' Association (IBA)**.

blocks.title: Genesis
rows: Created under the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007** to build a robust payment and settlement infrastructure.
Incorporated as a **'Not for Profit' company** under **Section 25 of the Companies Act 1956** (now **Section 8 of the Companies Act 2013**).
Provide infrastructure for the whole banking system for physical and electronic payment and settlement, bring technology-led innovation to retail payments, and widen their reach.

blocks.title: Where NPCI sits
items: Not-for-profit umbrella body for retail payments
UPI, RuPay, IMPS, BBPS, NACH, NFS, AePS

blocks.title: Promoter banks: 6-2-2
blocks.phrase: Six public, two private, two foreign: SPCBUB, then IH, then CH.
letters: SBI, PNB, Canara, Bank of Baroda, Union Bank, Bank of India
blocks.note: The first letters S-P-C-B-U-B follow the public sector list in order.

blocks.title: Section 25 became Section 8
blocks.text: NPCI was a Section 25 company under the 1956 Act. The same 'not for profit' provision is **Section 8** of the Companies Act 2013.

rows: A **bank-led model** that allows basic, interoperable banking transactions at a **PoS (Micro ATM)** through the **business correspondent of any bank**, using **Aadhaar authentication**. It is a network of Micro ATMs using Aadhaar authentication.
Balance enquiry, cash withdrawal, cash deposit and Aadhaar-to-Aadhaar fund transfer. A small overdraft facility is **not** one of them.
Aadhaar number, fingerprint (biometric) and the Issuer Identification Number of the bank.

A payment service of NPCI that uses the **Aadhaar number issued by UIDAI**. Government departments and agencies use it to transfer benefits and subsidies under **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** schemes.

blocks.title: AePS vs APBS
blocks.text: **AePS** is for customer banking transactions at a Micro ATM through a business correspondent. **APBS** is the government's channel for **DBT subsidy payments**.

**BBPS** is an integrated, **interoperable** bill payment system conceptualised by the **RBI** and driven by the **NPCI**. It is a one-stop ecosystem offering 'Anytime Anywhere' bill payment with certainty, reliability and safety. Customers get instant confirmation by SMS or receipt, and a mechanism to handle complaints is in place.

blocks.title: BBPS milestones
items: BBPS is conceptualised (the source says 'founded in 2013').
Launched by NPCI on the recommendation of the **G. Padmanabhan Committee** (RBI Executive Director).

blocks.title: How it works
rows: Electricity, telecom, DTH, gas, water and more through a single window. Possible additions: insurance premium, mutual funds, school and institution fees, credit cards, local taxes, invoice payments.
Internet, internet banking, mobile, mobile banking, mobile wallets, mPoS (mobile point of sale), kiosk, ATM, bank branch, agents and business correspondents.
Cards (credit, debit, prepaid), NEFT, internet banking, UPI, wallets, Aadhaar-based payments and cash (cheques also accepted).

blocks.title: Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication
rows: Used by over **11,000** banking and securities organisations in more than **200 countries**.
Also called an international money transfer: a secure and standardised way to send or receive money between banks anywhere in the world.
Institutions must declare compliance with **16 basic security principles** laid down by SWIFT to secure their access points to the network.
A standard format of Bank Identifier Code that identifies banks and financial institutions globally, generally 8 or 11 characters.

blocks.text: SWIFT is **Belgium-based**, started **May 1977**, owned by banks as a **non-profit cooperative**, and its code format is the **BIC**.

blocks.title: RTGS vs NEFT
rows: Funds move bank to bank on a **real-time** and **gross** basis
Nation-wide system letting individuals, firms and corporates transfer funds from any bank branch to any other bank branch
Primarily for **large-value** transactions; limits vary from bank to bank, so check with the bank
RBI extended it to non-bank payment operators such as Paytm, Visa, PhonePe and payments banks
RBI extended it to non-bank operators such as Paytm, Airtel wallet and payments banks

blocks.title: NEFT charges
items: NEFT initiated **online** through internet or mobile banking is **not chargeable**.
Through a banking channel (branch), a **maximum of ₹25** plus taxes is charged.

blocks.title: RTGS first, NEFT next
blocks.phrase: Oh-four RTGS, Oh-five NEFT: Real-time came in 2004, Electronic transfer in 2005.
blocks.note: NEFT became 24x7 first (2019), RTGS followed a year later (2020).

blocks.title: National Unified USSD Platform (NUUP)
rows: A **USSD-based mobile banking service** of NPCI, first launched in **November 2012**.
Takes banking to every common person; a common technology platform that lets banks and telecom service providers (TSPs) integrate to provide banking over **basic as well as smart phones**.

blocks.title: IFSC (Indian Financial System Code)
rows: An alphanumeric code that identifies a bank branch participating in NEFT.
**11 characters**: first 4 alphabetic characters = bank, last 6 = branch.

blocks.title: Electronic Clearing Service (ECS)
rows: The Reserve Bank of India; uses electronic payment instructions instead of paper instruments.
Lets companies pay interest or dividend to a large number of beneficiaries by direct credit to their bank accounts.
Collects charges for utilities such as electricity and telephone, insurance premiums and loan instalments directly from the customer's account.
Bulk transfer of funds from one account to many, or from many to one.

blocks.text: **UPI** is a real-time **inter-bank payment system** for sending or requesting money. It was developed by NPCI. Any UPI client app can be used, and **multiple bank accounts can be linked to a single app**. UPI is built on the IMPS infrastructure.

blocks.title: Ways to send or request money on UPI
rows: Send or request money to or from the bank account mapped to a Virtual Payment Address.
Send or request money using the account mapped to a mobile number.
Send money to the bank account (sending only).
Send money to the bank account mapped to an Aadhaar number.
Scan a QR that holds the VPA, account number and IFSC, or mobile number.

blocks.title: Five UPI routes: V-M-A-A-Q
blocks.phrase: Very Many Apps Are Quick: VPA, Mobile number, Account + IFSC, Aadhaar, QR code.

blocks.title: UPI Autopay
blocks.text: **UPI Autopay** was launched by NPCI in **August 2020**. It lets customers set up **recurring e-mandates** through any UPI app for mobile bills, EMI payments, OTT subscriptions, insurance and mutual funds.

**Bharat QR** enables digital payments and reduces the use of card-swiping machines. Several banks prepared for it before it was launched in **September 2016**, with the aim of moving India towards a **less-cash society**.

items: Works mainly by **scanning QR codes**, but also allows payment through an **Aadhaar number, UPI payment address, or account number with IFSC**.
Reduces the need to pay by debit and credit cards, which the source calls less secure than Bharat QR.
Supports **dynamic QR code** generation, so the payer need not enter the amount.
Supports **RuPay, Mastercard, Visa, American Express** and other national banks' cards.
Multiple cards can be linked to a Bharat QR supported bank app and any one chosen for a payment.
Offers a faster, secure payment mode with IMPS; there is no need to share mobile number, account details or CVV.

blocks.title: Bharat Interface for Money
rows: An Indian mobile payment app developed by NPCI, based on **UPI**.
Named after **B. R. Ambedkar**; launched on **30 December 2016**, as part of the push for cashless payments after the 2016 demonetisation.
Works with all Indian banks that use UPI; UPI itself is built over the **IMPS** infrastructure; usable on all mobile devices.
Send or receive money to or from UPI payment addresses, or to non-UPI accounts by scanning a QR with account number and IFSC, or with an **MMID** (Mobile Money Identifier).

blocks.title: BHIM is not a wallet
blocks.text: Mobile wallets such as Paytm, MobiKwik, mPesa and Airtel Money **hold money**. BHIM only **moves money between bank accounts**.

blocks.title: The 2016 trio
blocks.phrase: 2016 = Bills, QR, BHIM: BBPS 31 August, Bharat QR September, BHIM 30 December (Ambedkar).
blocks.note: All three arrived in the same year as demonetisation (2016).

blocks.title: Cheque Truncation System (CTS)
rows: Stopping the flow of the physical cheque from the drawer's side to the drawee branch. An **electronic image** of the cheque is sent instead, along with MICR fields, date of presentation and presenting bank details.
Removes the need to move physical cheques across branches, except in exceptional cases.

blocks.title: Immediate Payment Service (IMPS)
rows: An **instant inter-bank electronic funds transfer** service through mobile phones.
**24x7** throughout the year, including bank holidays, unlike RTGS.

blocks.title: National Automated Clearing House (NACH)
rows: A **centralised clearing service** introduced by NPCI for inter-bank, **high-volume, low-value** transactions that are **repetitive and periodic**.
Credit and debit services for corporates, banks and financial institutions.
Integrate all regional ECS systems into **one national payment system**; it is claimed to be better than its predecessor, ECS.

blocks.text: The **NFS** is the **largest domestic ATM network** in India and a leader in providing inter-bank ATM services to the maximum number of customers.

blocks.title: Card-to-card fund transfer (value-added service)
rows: A cardholder of a participating NFS member bank sends funds to another cardholder of a participating member bank, using the **beneficiary's card number**, typed in by the remitter.
Interoperable, instant, available 24/7, paperless, secure and better fund management.

blocks.text: **RuPay** enables electronic payments at all Indian banks and financial institutions. It was conceived and launched by NPCI on **26 March 2012**. To help RuPay gain international acceptance, NPCI maintains ties with **Discover Financial** and **JCB**.

blocks.title: Benefits of RuPay
items: International transactions raise costs; processing **within the country** with RuPay reduces these costs.
Processing fees are **considerably lower** than for regular debit or credit cards.

blocks.text: RuPay: launched by NPCI on 26 March 2012; international ties with **Discover Financial** and **JCB**; domestic processing keeps costs lower.

blocks.title: Two 2012 launches
blocks.note: Both NPCI products date from 2012; RuPay's tie-ups are Discover Financial and JCB.

revision: NPCI is the umbrella organisation for retail payments, set up with RBI and IBA support under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
NPCI is a not-for-profit company: Section 25 of Companies Act 1956, now Section 8 of Companies Act 2013.
10 promoter banks: SBI, PNB, Canara, Bank of Baroda, Union Bank, Bank of India, ICICI, HDFC, Citibank and HSBC.
AePS: bank-led, Aadhaar-authenticated transactions at Micro ATMs through business correspondents; APBS is used for DBT subsidies.
BBPS: RBI conceptualised, NPCI driven, launched 31 August 2016 on G. Padmanabhan Committee advice; 24x7x365.
SWIFT: Belgium-based, bank-owned non-profit cooperative society, operational since May 1977, used in 200+ countries.
RTGS opened 29 April 2004 (24x7 from 4 Dec 2020); NEFT introduced November 2005 (24x7 from Dec 2019, no limit).
NUUP (*99#) was launched in November 2012 as a USSD-based mobile banking service.
IFSC has 11 characters: 4 alphabetic for the bank and 6 for the branch.
UPI sends or requests money using VPA, mobile number, account plus IFSC, Aadhaar or QR; UPI Autopay began August 2020.
Bharat QR launched September 2016; supports RuPay, Mastercard, Visa and Amex.
BHIM: named after B. R. Ambedkar, launched 30 December 2016, built on UPI; it moves money between bank accounts and is not a wallet.
CTS sends a cheque image instead of the physical cheque; IMPS is 24x7 instant transfer via mobile.
NACH is a centralised clearing service for high-volume, low-value repetitive payments and replaces regional ECS.
NFS is the largest domestic ATM network; RuPay launched 26 March 2012 with Discover Financial and JCB ties.
